==========================================================
 Kevaram Nimbaram Rabari
 Versus
 Barkatali Ahmedbhai Musla & Ors.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 Mr Dharm K Raval(10689) for the Appellant(s) No. 1
 Mr Rathin P Raval(5013) for the Defendant(s) No. 3
 Rule Served for the Defendant(s) No. 1,2
 ==========================================================
 Coram:Honourable Mr. Justice Sandeep N. Bhatt
 Date : 13/09/2024
 Oral Order

1. The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellant/s - original claimant/s, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgments and awards dated 29.04.2022 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Deesa in Motor Accident Claim Petitions No.3972 & 3973 of 2009, by which the Tribunal has dismissed both the claim petitions.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claim Petitions No.3972 & 3973 of 2009
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. Heard learned advocates.
3.

Learned advocate for the appellant/s - original claimant/s has submitted that the Tribunal has dismissed both the claim petitions on technical grounds, which NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2117/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined frustrates the object of the Motor Vehicles Act.

He has further submitted that the Tribunal has not considered the Panchnama at Kevaram Nimbaram Rabari vs Barkatali Ahmedbhai Musla on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189124978/
1 Exh.40 and complaint lodged by the owner of the vehicle at Exh.39 in its true spirit; and that the Tribunal has not considered the version of the complaint Exh.39; and that the Tribunal has erred while coming to conclusion that complaint at Exh.39 given by the owner is doubtful in absence of material facts and evidence.

entities.text: Panchnama at Kevaram Nimbaram Rabari vs Barkatali Ahmedbhai Musla
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has submitted that both the matters may be remanded back to the Tribunal concerned for fresh adjudication after giving proper opportunities to adduce and produce the relevant and necessary evidence, within reasonable time.
4. Learned advocate Mr. Rathin Raval for the respondent - insurance company has submitted that the Tribunal has rightly passed the impugned judgment and award.
He has submitted that the Tribunal has considered all the relevant documents available on record and dismissed the claim petitions.
He has submitted that even otherwise, appropriate order may be passed.

5. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act are benevolent legislation and normally, it should be construed that the provisions of the Act are enacted to see that the claimants could get some amount of compensation where the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2117/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined claimants either lose their bread-earner or has received serious injuries.
There cannot be any perfect arithmetic calculation for awarding amount of calculation.

Further, considering Sections 166, 167 ad 168 of the Act, the object of the M.V. Act and the various judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court whereby it is observed that the Court should try to give proper meaning to the provisions of the Act in such cases filed under the Act and such claim petitions, normally, should not be rejected by taking hyper technical view and if sufficient material is available on the record of the Tribunal or Court, the Tribunal shall consider the such claim petition/s on its own merits instead of dismissing such claim petition/s by taking hyper technical view and by asking for strict proof about the cause of the accident and involvement of the vehicle.
It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
The concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.
It also endeavors to make good the human suffering to the extent possible and to also save families which have lost their breadwinners from being pushed to wandering.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2117/2023 ORDER DATED: 13/09/2024 undefined 6.

Under the circumstances, the ends of justice would meet, if the matters are required to be remanded back to the concerned Tribunal for fresh consideration, after giving proper opportunities to the parties to adduce and produce the relevant and necessary evidence on record, within reasonable period, in accordance with law.
7. In view of above, the following order is passed.

7.1 The impugned judgments and awards dated 29.04.2022 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Deesa in Motor Accident Claim Petitions No.3972 & 3973 of 2009 are hereby quashed and set aside.
